<p>AWS Graviton5-based R9g database instances are now generally available for Amazon Aurora with PostgreSQL compatibility and MySQL compatibility, and for Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MariaDB.<br> &nbsp;<br> Graviton5-based R9g instances provide up to a 30% performance improvement and up to a 22% price-performance improvement for on-demand pricing over Graviton4-based instances of equivalent sizes on Amazon Aurora, depending on database engine, version, and workload. items.descriptionHtml: <p>Today, AWS Quick is announcing the general availability of structured data connector restrictions through custom permissions. items.descriptionHtml: <p>AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store now supports 13 new parameter data types that automatically validate parameter values when you create or update a parameter. With built-in validation, you can stop malformed configuration values, such as an invalid IP address, AWS account ID, or JSON document, before your applications read them, without writing your own validation logic.&nbsp;These types allow you to better organize your parameters across your workloads. You can filter by type when calling the DescribeParameters API or when browsing parameters in the Parameter Store console.<br> <br> The following data types are available for both standard and advanced parameters:&nbsp; aws:region, aws:account:id, boolean, integer, float, binary, hostname, email, ipv4-address, and ipv6-address. Three more data types, url, json, and jsonc, are available for advanced parameters. Parameter Store checks the value when you call PutParameter and rejects any value that doesn't match its data type. New data types work with String and SecureString parameters, and several also support StringList parameters, where each item in the list is validated. You can combine a data type with an AllowedPattern for additional constraints, and you can change the data type of an existing text parameter.</p>

items.descriptionHtml: <p><a href="https://aws.amazon.com/ecs/">Amazon Elastic Container Service</a> (Amazon ECS) introduces json-file log driver support for Amazon ECS Managed Instances and log driver volumes for Amazon ECS Managed Daemons. Together, these features let you collect application logs with the observability agent of your choice and forward them to any destination you choose.<br> <br> With this launch, your application containers on ECS Managed Instances can write their logs as local files in standard Docker json-file format, which most observability agents read natively. Your managed daemons can directly read these files through a volume mount, without specifying host bind mount paths or requiring root privileges. As a result, one managed daemon on each instance can collect logs from every application container that uses the json-file log driver. Amazon ECS keeps each container's logs in a dedicated directory named with the container ID and retains them until the container is removed, so your managed daemon can use native file-based log collection and trace every log back to the container that produced it.<br> <br> To get started, set the log driver to json-file in the logConfiguration of your application task definition. Next, register a daemon task definition that specifies a volume with logDriverVolumeConfiguration, and mount the volume into your daemon container using mountPoints. You can configure this using the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, API, AWS SDKs or AWS CloudFormation. This feature is available in all commercial AWS Regions where Amazon ECS Managed Instances and Managed Daemons are available, at no additional cost. To learn more, refer to our <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/managed-daemons-task-definitions.html#managed-daemons-volumes">documentation</a> page and visit <a href="https://aws.amazon.com/ecs/managed-instances/">Amazon ECS Managed Instances</a>.</p>

items.descriptionHtml: <p>AWS WAF announces automatic SDK integration for Amazon CloudFront distributions. <p>Amazon SageMaker AI serverless model customization now supports training session APIs, giving customers full control over their post-training algorithm without provisioning or managing GPU infrastructure. Managed techniques, including SFT, DPO, and other reinforcement learning methods, let customers pick a technique and a model and have SageMaker AI run the training. SageMaker AI is also releasing the <a href="https://github.com/aws/sagemaker-training-sessions-cookbook">SageMaker training sessions cookbook</a>, a set of ready-to-run SFT and RL recipes customers can use as blueprints for their own training loops.<a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/customizing-models-training-sessions.html"></a></p> 
<p>Training session APIs are generally available today in US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), and Asia Pacific (Mumbai). items.descriptionHtml: <p>IAM Identity Center helps you configure the single sign-on experience of your workforce to AWS accounts and applications. You can now use optimistic locking for users and groups in the identity store, so that update and delete requests succeed only if the user or group hasn't changed since you last read it. This helps when multiple administrators or automated workflows modify the same user or group at nearly the same time, where previously one write could silently overwrite another.<br> <br> Each user and group now has a Revision value that changes every time the user's or group's attributes are modified, including through SCIM provisioning, Active Directory sync, or the IAM Identity Center console. Create, describe, update, and list operations return the current Revision, and you can pass it on a later UpdateUser, UpdateGroup, DeleteUser, or DeleteGroup request. The request succeeds only if the supplied Revision matches the current Revision. Otherwise, it returns a ConflictException, so your workflow can re-read the user or group and retry with the latest values.<br> <br> Providing a Revision is optional. Requests that omit it behave as before, so existing integrations continue to work without changes. Conditional requests are supported through the Identity Store API, not the SCIM endpoint. Group membership operations don't accept a Revision, and adding or removing members doesn't change the Revision of the user or the group. This capability is available in all AWS Regions where IAM Identity Center is available. IAM Identity Center is provided at no additional cost.<br> <br> To learn more about IAM Identity Center, visit the product detail page. To get started, see UpdateUser in the <a title="identity store update user API" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/IdentityStoreAPIReference/API_UpdateUser.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Identity Store API Reference</a>.</p>

items.descriptionHtml: <p>AWS End User Messaging now makes it easier to complete messaging registrations correctly the first time, with clearer guidance, explicit field requirements, and help avoiding the most common rejection reasons. Registrations ask for compliance evidence such as opt-in proof and sample messages, and submissions are often delayed or denied when that evidence is incomplete or a required field is missed. These improvements give you worked examples, surface exactly which fields you must provide, and walk you through the content that most often causes denials.<br> <br> First, example mock-ups of a compliant opt-in and sample messages are now included for US 10DLC, US short code, US toll-free and RCS registrations, so you can see what a compliant submission looks like before you build your own. Second, the registration API response now surfaces conditional logic, so you and your AI agents no longer have to guess which fields are required based on other field values. The response tells you which fields are required for your specific registration. Third, RCS registration now includes a walkthrough for recording the compliant video that agent registrations require.<br> <br> These improvements are available in all Regions where AWS End User Messaging registrations are available.<br> <br> To learn more and get started, see the End User Messaging <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/end-user-messaging/latest/userguide/nx-overview.html">User Guide</a>.</p>

items.descriptionHtml: <p>Today, AWS End User Messaging announces Brand Profiles, which let you store your brand and company information once and reuse it across your messaging registrations. To send messages on SMS, RCS, and WhatsApp, you register your brand with carriers and messaging providers, and today you fill in the same company details, address, contact information, and use case by hand on every form, for each channel and country. That repeated entry slows every new registration, and a typo or other error can get one rejected and delay when you can start sending. With Brand Profiles, you enter this information once and apply it to each new registration, so you register faster and keep your details consistent across channels and countries. You can use Brand Profiles whether you send for your own brand or manage several brands in a single AWS account.<br> <br> When you start a registration with a Brand Profile, the service fills in the matching fields from the information you saved and gives you a draft to review before you submit. By default, it matches standard fields such as company name, tax ID, address, and contact details. You can also turn on smart match, which uses AI to fill in fields even when their names differ. You can build a Brand Profile from scratch or start from your existing registrations.<br> <br> Brand Profiles is available in all commercial AWS Regions where AWS End User Messaging is available.<br> <br> To learn more and get started, see the AWS End User Messaging <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/end-user-messaging/latest/userguide/nx-features-brand-profiles.html">User Guide.</a></p>

items.descriptionHtml: <p>Today, AWS End User Messaging announces end-to-end managed one-time passcode (OTP) verification in Notify. You get a working OTP solution in under five minutes, including AWS phone numbers and code verification, without setting up a phone number, registering with carriers, or managing how messages are delivered. Before, you generated the passcode yourself and passed it to Notify to send, and you built and maintained the logic to create, store, and expire codes. Now Notify generates the code, delivers it, and verifies the code the recipient enters, so you ship a complete verification flow and skip that work entirely. You can deliver codes over text, voice, and now WhatsApp.<br> <br> You set the rules once in a notify code configuration: the code type, length, how long it stays valid, and how many attempts a recipient gets, along with your templates for each channel. From then on, one call sends a code to a recipient on the channel you choose, and another checks the code they enter.<br> <br> Notify is available in all commercial AWS Regions where AWS End User Messaging is available.<br> <br> To learn more and get started, see the AWS End User Messaging <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/end-user-messaging/latest/userguide/nx-notify.html">User Guide.</a></p>

items.descriptionHtml:
<p>Amazon Redshift now supports querying Amazon S3 data lake tables located in a different AWS Region. With enhanced VPC routing, data lake query traffic between Amazon S3 and Amazon Redshift stays within your own VPC.&nbsp;Both capabilities are powered by the integrated data lake query engine that runs directly on the compute of RG provisioned and Serverless clusters. These features are aimed at enterprises with globally distributed data and at security-sensitive customers who need tight control over how their data travels.</p>
<p>With cross-Region support, you can use Amazon Redshift to query S3 data in another Region directly, without first copying or replicating it. This makes it easier to run global analytics, consolidate reporting across Regions, and query data that must remain in a specific Region for residency requirements. Cross-Region queries incur standard data transfer charges. Because the query engine runs on your cluster's compute, data moving between Amazon S3 and Amazon Redshift flows entirely over your VPC when you use enhanced VPC routing, never over public networks. Regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare, and government benefit from this feature as it keeps data lake queries within the network boundaries their compliance requirements demand.&nbsp;&nbsp;Both capabilities work with the integrated data lake query engine, which is available in all regions where RG provisioned and Serverless clusters are available. To learn more, see <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/mgmt/spectrum-enhanced-vpc.html#spectrum-enhanced-vpc-integrated-engine"><u>Querying your data lake</u>&nbsp;tables with enhanced VPC routing</a>&nbsp;in the <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/" style="background-color: rgb(255,255,255);">Amazon Redshift documentation</a>.</p>
